transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jared Chen (Redwood CSM), Nina Patel (AstraHealth Head of ML), Samir Khan (Infra Lead), Olivia Park (Product)

Summary (auto): quick bench review, talk about tuning (batching, quantize profile), plan on-prem run

00:00 Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check, is this still the right agenda, run through numbers, talk tuning, next steps?
00:08 Nina: yep that's perfect, thanks Lena, we mostly want the latency p95/p99 numbers vs what we're seeing from FastServe and then some notes on reliability.
00:20 Marco: great, so we have the latest sheet up, benchmark-results.csv — I'll share in chat after — we ran three workloads: short prompts (<=64 tokens), medium (256), and long (512) at 1% sampling for p95/p99.
00:35 Marco: headline — on our dedicated pool with KV caching enabled we hit median token latency ~18ms, p95 about 120ms for 256 token runs, and throughput about 310 rps sustained. FastServe baseline for the same hardware profile was p95 ~160ms and throughput ~220 rps.
00:55 Samir: wait are those numbers for single-instance or multi-node? I thought your dedicated pool was autoscaled to 4 nodes for these tests?
01:02 Marco: yeah good question, tests ran on a 3-node dedicated cluster (NVIDIA H100 equivalent), with auto-burst set off so we're looking at steady state. For single-node numbers we saw throughput ~140 rps, p95 ~210ms.
01:20 Olivia: curious about cold-starts — when traffic drops to zero and comes back, what's the latency bump?
01:26 Marco: cold starts depend on model warm state & KV cache. Cold start for a 512 prompt was around 450-600ms for the first request, then it drops once the KV cache warms up. We instrumented cache hits vs misses — with prefix caching configured we get ~75% hit rate within 30 seconds for repeated sessions.
01:45 Nina: that KV cash spelling — you mean KV cache, right?
01:47 Marco: yes, sorry KV cache — transcription thing — we noticed a small transcription typo.
01:52 Lena: also to call out, we ran quantized profile Q4 and Q8 for the 512 tests, Q4 gave slightly lower throughput but better memory fit, Q8 was best for latency.
02:10 Samir: what about CPU host saturation — we had issues on our infra with CPU spiking when requests hit the host network stack. Any mitigation?
02:20 Marco: we observed host CPU spikes when batching was set too high; lowering max batch size and using our smart routing to keep latency SLOs helped. Also enabling direct NIC offload and pinning interrupts dropped CPU by ~12%. We'll include those kernel tuning notes in the runbook.
02:39 Nina: how reproducible are the numbers? We ran our baseline across multiple AZs and saw variance ~10-15%.
02:46 Marco: our numbers are aggregated across three runs, variance was about 8% p95 for medium prompts. We can provide raw traces and the run script.
03:02 Olivia: any differences in tokenization or prompt pre/post processing that could skew latency?
03:08 Marco: good call — we've aligned tokenization to your service (we used the same tokenizer settings), but post-processing (safety filters, reranking) can add 30-60ms depending on mode. In these tests we disabled extra post-processing to isolate raw generation latency.
03:30 Nina: and error rates? Did you observe retries or throttled spikes?
03:34 Marco: error rate was <0.1% in steady state; the baseline saw higher retry rates during sustained load (0.6–1.2%). We traced bursts to their autoscaler config.
03:50 Samir: on the security front we need SOC2 type II, SAML SSO, audit logs with retention; is that in your private deployment?
03:58 Lena: yes, Redwood Private supports SSO, detailed audit logs, and we have SOC2 and ISO docs — I'll send the security pack (redwood-security-pack.pdf). For on-prem we also support customer-managed KMS/HSM.
04:15 Nina: can you also confirm data residency options? We need EU region for some PHI tests.
04:21 Lena: yes EU region is available, and Private can be deployed in customer's VPC for residency. We'll include region endpoints in the follow-up.
04:32 Marco: back to perf, one tuning we recommend is queue length tuning per model and a dynamic batching profile; for your 512 workload we reduced max_batch to 24 which kept p95 lower while preserving throughput.
04:45 Nina: is there a tradeoff chart you can share for batch size vs p95?
04:49 Marco: yes that's in the slides; I'll export the chart and the csv.
05:00 Olivia: for the on-prem run, network egress will matter — how did you measure network latency contributions?
05:06 Marco: we instrumented kernel-level RTT and did client-to-host pings; network contributed roughly 15–25ms for our cross-AZ runs. Local on-prem should be lower.
05:20 Jared: we also noticed that enabling our persistent KV cache for prompt prefixes gave the biggest wins for repeated sessions — up to 35% lower p95 for medium prompts.
05:33 Samir: can you do a sustained 24h run on a dedicated cluster? That'd show heat/GC/thermals and realistic autoscaler behavior.
05:40 Marco: yes we will schedule a 24h sustained run and send logs. We'll also collect p99 tail to compare with your baseline.
05:50 Lena: ok recap — Marco to run 24h sustained test and share logs; Nina to send prompt sets; Lena to send security docs and updated pricing. Any other items?
05:58 Nina: none from me, thanks team.
06:02 Lena: cool thanks all, we'll follow up in email and update the sheet. Meeting end.

References and artifacts: benchmark-results.csv (shared), redwood-security-pack.pdf (link), runbook-kernel-tuning.md (link).

Notes: occasional transcription errors (KV cash), speaker labels genericized, some timestamps approximate.
